skill.name: set-up-tracking
skill.description: Set up Product Metrics server-side conversion tracking end to end for a store owner, with the productmetrics CLI or the Product Metrics MCP server (search and execute tools): sign in, create or pick the workspace, connect the store (Shopify, WooCommerce, Shopware, Lightspeed, Magento or any website through Cloudflare Tracking), connect Google Ads and Meta, create the conversion actions, set consent and additional costs, and confirm the first purchase arrives. Use it when someone asks to "set up Product Metrics", "install tracking", "connect my store", "start sending profit to Google Ads", or asks what is left to set up. Browser steps (Google consent, Shopify approval, checkout, Cloudflare sign-in) are handed to the person as a URL.
skill.summary: Set up server-side purchase tracking with Product Metrics and verify a paid test order.
skill.author: product-metrics

security_audit.summary: The backtick and reconnaissance matches are Markdown syntax or normal account setup, but the Product Metrics MCP URL is a live external endpoint. The workflow exposes credentials and lacks explicit checks for tool permissions, browser links, and consent readiness. No evidence of malware, prompt injection, or covert data transfer was found in the reviewed file.

remediation.issue: Credentials and setup tokens enter the assistant workflow.
remediation.suggestion: Send users to the provider app for secret entry. Keep secrets out of chat, CLI arguments, tool output, and diagnostic messages.

remediation.issue: Connector permissions and write approvals are not scoped to the task.
remediation.suggestion: Keep status checks read-only. Before writes, confirm the workspace, storefront, destination, and change, then request only the connector permissions needed.

remediation.issue: CLI examples do not specify safe argument handling.
remediation.suggestion: Pass names, URLs, and IDs as separate arguments without a shell, or use structured MCP parameters. Validate provider-specific IDs and URLs.

remediation.issue: Browser handoffs trust returned URLs without validation.
remediation.suggestion: Check HTTPS and the expected provider or verified store domain before sharing authorization and checkout links. Avoid exposing session-bearing URLs in logs.

remediation.issue: Consent readiness is not checked before activation or purchase testing.
remediation.suggestion: Confirm the store consent configuration and applicable platform terms before enabling event delivery or testing with a paid order.

semantic_findings.title: Credentials Exposed to Assistant and CLI
semantic_findings.description: The skill asks users for Lightspeed and Meta secrets and passes them as CLI arguments. It also reveals store setup tokens in tool output.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instructions and examples explicitly put secrets in assistant input, process arguments, or tool output. Avoiding repetition does not prevent capture in transcripts or logs.

semantic_findings.title: Broad Connector Permissions and Unconfirmed Writes
semantic_findings.description: The skill asks users to reauthorize the connector with read, setup, and write access. It does not separate status-only requests from authorization for routine writes.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The reconnect rule requests all three permissions, and later steps assign properties or enable destinations without a distinct approval. Browser approvals and delete checks remain explicit.

semantic_findings.title: Shell Templates Lack Safe Argument Boundaries
semantic_findings.description: Bash examples include user-provided names and store URLs but do not require separate arguments. Substituting those values into shell text can change how the shell interprets them.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The examples place variable values in Bash command text. Exposure depends on whether the agent uses a shell or passes arguments separately.

semantic_findings.title: Unvalidated Authorization and Checkout Links
semantic_findings.description: The skill presents returned browser URLs as trusted steps for sign-in, authorization, or checkout without checking their destination.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The handoff lacks an HTTPS or expected-domain check. The phishing risk depends on a compromised or malformed response, not a known malicious link.

semantic_findings.title: Consent Readiness Not Verified Before Event Delivery
semantic_findings.description: Store activation and conversion creation precede manual consent configuration. Later steps enable Meta and request a paid test order without verifying consent readiness.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The guide names manual consent and data terms but does not make their completion a prerequisite. The service's own enforcement is not shown.

content.value_statement: Conversion tracking requires setup across your storefront, ad accounts, and consent tools. Use Product Metrics to connect those services, identify manual steps, and check a paid test order.
actual_capabilities: Reads Product Metrics onboarding status and creates a workspace for an owner when needed.
Connects supported storefronts or creates a website installation for Cloudflare Tracking.
Connects a selected Google Ads account and links a storefront installation to its property.
Creates and verifies secondary Google Ads conversion actions.
Configures and tests an optional Meta Conversions API destination.
Checks whether a paid test order reached Product Metrics and reports remaining setup steps.
limitations: Requires an authenticated Product Metrics CLI or MCP connection for account operations.
Users complete browser approvals, checkout, store admin tasks, consent configuration, and additional costs in the relevant app.
The skill does not change primary bidding goals. Magento requires a developer to install the module and the owner to use the app.
Except for Shopify, the documented connection flow requires a Pro subscription. Shopify billing runs through its app.

prompt_templates.prompt: Check the secondary conversion actions for my Google Ads property. List what is missing and ask before creating anything. Leave bidding settings unchanged.

prompt_templates.scenario: Validate an existing setup before relying on it for ad reporting.

output_examples.input: What still needs setup for my Shopify store?
output: The workspace and Google Ads property are connected.
The Shopify connection is waiting for app approval. Enable and save the Product Metrics app embed in the Shopify theme editor after approval.
No purchase has been verified yet.

output_examples.input: Did the Cloudflare test order arrive, and did bidding change?
output: Product Metrics received paid test order 1042 for USD 24.00.
The Google Ads conversion actions are secondary. No bidding settings were changed.

best_practices: Confirm the exact workspace, storefront, and destination account before authorizing a change.
Enter credentials and copy setup tokens in the provider dashboard rather than sharing them in chat.
Verify consent configuration before testing and check the test order in the intended storefront.
anti_patterns: Granting write access when you only need to check setup status.
Choosing a Google Ads manager account instead of the client account that runs the campaigns.
Treating a successful Product Metrics purchase check as proof that every ad destination accepted the event.

faq.question: Which tools can run this skill?
faq.answer: Use Claude, Codex, or Claude Code with access to the Product Metrics CLI or an authenticated Product Metrics MCP connector.

faq.question: Which storefronts are supported?
faq.answer: The guide covers Shopify, WooCommerce, Shopware 6, Lightspeed C-Series, and Magento. Other websites can use Cloudflare Tracking with a verified domain.

faq.question: Can the skill accept permissions or pay for a subscription?
faq.answer: No. You complete browser approvals and checkout yourself. Product Metrics checkout requires a workspace admin.

faq.question: Will the skill change Google Ads bidding?
faq.answer: No. It creates secondary conversion actions. You choose whether to make one primary in Google Ads.

faq.question: When does Product Metrics send profit data?
faq.answer: Profit is sent only after you activate additional costs. Cloudflare Tracking also requires a product cost fallback setting.

faq.question: Does a test purchase prove both ad platforms received it?
faq.answer: No. The purchase check confirms receipt in Product Metrics. Use destination-specific checks to confirm event delivery.
